divergences.topic: Fee (ujrah) on kafalah — may a guarantor charge?
divergences.why_it_matters: The Kafalah demo's showcase scenario: same contract, divergent living answers.
standard_refs: CBUAE HSA Resolution: fees for Letters of Guarantee/Credit (Kafalah)

positions.position: Not permissible to take remuneration for issuing a letter of guarantee, with or without cover, where the remuneration is consideration for the guarantee itself (expense recovery treated separately).
positions.basis: SS 5 text read verbatim from ss1.txt 2026-07-18

positions.position: Permits the fee: the guarantor may charge for the kafalah service, as a fixed amount or a percentage of the guaranteed amount.
Dedicated HSA resolution on fees for Letters of Guarantee/Credit exists; position recorded when the document is downloaded.
Classical Hanafi architecture of kafalah (Kasani, Bada'i) treats it in the guarantee framework the AAOIFI prohibition rests on; explicit school-level fee statement pending a direct citation.
positions.basis: kafalah_v4.json K016 (structure only — fee statement not in the quoted passage)

positions.position: Classical Hanbali treatment (Ibn Qudama, al-Mughni 5:71) records the guarantee's validity across schools; explicit fee statement pending a direct citation.

divergences.why_it_matters: The most contested liquidity tool; bodies and jurisdictions genuinely split.

positions.position: Resolution 179 (19/5), Sharjah, April 2009: organized and reverse (banking) tawarruq impermissible; classical form permitted with conditions.
Permitted but restricted: need-based, not a financing mode of first resort; commodity must be sold to a third party — 'inah strictly prohibited (4/5).
Commodity-murabaha platforms operate at scale; regulatory position recorded when SC documents are downloaded.
Contested WITHIN the school: individual tawarruq recorded/permitted in later Hanbali manuals (al-Bahuti, Sharh Muntaha); opposed by Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim.

divergences.topic: Late-payment charge — income for the bank, or charity only?
divergences.why_it_matters: Every deferred-sale demo must show where a late fee goes.

positions.position: Any charity payment against defaults and delayed payments by the customer shall not be recognised as an income of the seller and shall be taken directly to charity payable, when received.

divergences.topic: Ijarah ending in ownership — is the transfer a separate contract from the lease?
divergences.why_it_matters: Lease-to-own demo: rent versus ownership must stay separate.

positions.position: Such transfer of the ownership is executed through a sale or a gift, or a series of sales transactions – independent of Ijarah contract.
Ijarah rentals do not include any consideration paid or promised for transfer of ownership or proportionate ownership, either as lump sum or as a gradual payment or as a residual value guarantee.

divergences.topic: Sukuk — asset-backed (real transfer, no recourse) vs asset-based (market norm)
divergences.why_it_matters: The core sukuk trust question: do holders own the asset or just the credit?

positions.position: The SPV must not have any recourse to the originator for compensation of losses generated from the Sukuk assets, unless there is a Shari'ah compliant arrangement for credit enhancement in the structure of the Sukuk transaction duly approved by SSSB.

...it is necessary to introduce such a requirement and move towards practices that truly reflect the objectives of Shari'ah as well as governance principles ... and do not merely endorse current market practices which is normally asset-based Sukuk.
positions.basis: GS 12 Basis for Conclusions BC15, read verbatim 2026-07-20 (2e410498-AAOIFIGS12SukukGovernance...txt)
